items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 only says 'square plate'; Sec. 4.1 says 'The length is fixed at L = 1.0 m' for all three problems of Fig. 6, but which dimension of Fig. 6a is labelled L is visible only in the figure. Because ℓ = 0.008 and h_min/h_max are absolute lengths, the side length changes the effective regularization scale.
readings: side = L: 1.0 m × 1.0 m
side = 2L: 2.0 m × 2.0 m

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1: 'being fixed at Γ_u as shown in Fig. (6a)'. Which edge(s), and which part of them, is clamped appears only in the figure. Eq. 39 does state the support type (u = 0, both components). Coordinates: x from the left edge, y from the bottom edge, as fractions of the side L.
readings: entire left edge (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ L) clamped
entire top edge (y = L, 0 ≤ x ≤ L) clamped
entire bottom edge (y = 0) clamped
only the central part of the left edge (0.25L ≤ y ≤ 0.75L) clamped
two short segments (≈0.05L) at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners clamped

items.description: The Fig. 6 caption and Sec. 4.1.1 only say 'asymmetrically loaded'. Which edge carries Γ_t, and where along it (off the symmetry axis of the support), is shown only in Fig. 6a. Positions use x from the left edge and y from the bottom edge, as fractions of L.
readings: bottom-right corner (x = L, y = 0)
right edge at y = 0.25L
right edge at y = 0.75L
bottom edge at x = 0.75L
top edge at x = 0.75L

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the magnitude |t| = 1.0×10^3 N/m. The direction of t in problem (a) is only drawn in Fig. 6a; an inclined load could itself be the source of the 'asymmetry'.
readings: vertical, downward (−y)
horizontal (+x or −x)
inclined at 45° to the loaded edge

items.entity: length/distribution of the loaded segment Γ_t
items.description: The load is a boundary traction on a segment Γ_t (Eq. 39, units N/m), and φ = 1 is also imposed there, but the segment length is never stated (it may only be drawn in Fig. 6a). On a structured grid one must choose between a point load and a uniform traction over some number of element edges.
readings: concentrated force at a single node
uniform traction over a segment of length 0.02L
uniform traction over a segment of length 0.05L
uniform traction over a segment of length 0.1L

items.description: Sec. 4.1: '|t| = 1.0×10^3 N/m'. In a 2-D model a traction given in N/m produces a resultant that depends on the unknown length of Γ_t (and on thickness). The value can also be read as the total force per unit depth.
readings: uniform traction of 1.0e3 (N/m) over Γ_t, so the resultant = 1.0e3 × |Γ_t| per unit depth
resultant force of 1.0e3 N per unit depth applied at/over Γ_t

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2-D 'plate' (Sec. 4.1/4.1.1). Under plane strain the model is per unit depth; under plane stress the thickness scales the stiffness.
readings: unit thickness (1 m, i.e. per unit depth)
thin plate, e.g. 0.01 m, under plane stress

items.entity: 2-D constitutive assumption (plane strain vs plane stress)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 defines the Lamé constants 'in plane strain assumption', and Sec. 4.3 explicitly switches to plane stress for the L-bracket. Sec. 4.1/4.1.1 restate neither, and the structure is called a 'plate'. Plane strain is the default reading but is not confirmed for this example.
readings: plane strain: λ = Eν/((1+ν)(1−2ν)), μ = E/(2(1+ν)) (Sec. 2.1)
plane stress: λ* = Eν/(1−ν²), μ = E/(2(1+ν))

items.entity: forced-solid region at the load (level-set Dirichlet condition on 𝒢_t)
items.description: The evolution problem (Sec. 2.2, Sec. 3, A.2–A.5) imposes φ = 1 on 𝒢_t, which keeps the loaded boundary solid. But Appendix A.1, the standard wave equation used in Sec. 4.1.1, writes φ_{v+1} = 0 on 𝒢_t in its weak form. 𝒢_t is never defined explicitly (presumably the image of Γ_t), and the depth of the resulting non-design region on an element grid is not specified. No passive region is mentioned at Γ_u.
readings: φ = 1 on Γ_t, realized as one row of solid passive elements along the loaded segment
φ = 1 on Γ_t, realized as a small solid patch (e.g. 0.02L × 0.02L) around the load
φ = 0 on Γ_t (Appendix A.1): loaded edge kept on the material/void interface, no passive solid
no passive region at all

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only an adaptive FreeFEM++/mmg size range, h_min = 5×10^-4 to h_max = 1.0×10^-2 (no units, presumably m), with no adaptation metric or frequency. A uniform grid size is therefore undetermined. Because ℓ = 0.008 < h_max, the resolution relative to ℓ matters.
readings: 100 × 100 elements (h = 0.01 = h_max)

items.entity: element type / interpolation order for u and φ
items.description: Sec. 3 only says FreeFEM++ finite elements are used. The text gives neither the interpolation order of the displacement and level-set fields (P1/P2) nor how Θ(φ) enters the element stiffness. A structured-grid solver must choose, e.g., Q4 elements with element-wise Θ.
readings: P1 triangles for both u and φ
P2 for u, P1 for φ
bilinear Q4, Θ evaluated per element from the element-centre φ
bilinear Q4, Θ evaluated at Gauss points from nodal φ

items.description: No density or sensitivity filter is used. The only length scale is ℓ = 0.008 (stated to have length units, presumably m) in the wave-equation update with Δv = 1 (Sec. 3, A.1, Sec. 4.1.1). A conventional structured-grid compliance solver needs either this update or an equivalent filter, whose radius is not given.
readings: implement the paper's update φ_{v+1} − ℓ²∇²φ_{v+1} = −S_v + 2φ_v − φ_{v−1} with ℓ = 0.008 m
Helmholtz/PDE filter with length parameter ℓ = 0.008 m
density/sensitivity filter radius R = 2√3·ℓ ≈ 0.028 m
density/sensitivity filter radius R = ℓ = 0.008 m

items.entity: set of β values in the study
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says β is 'varied between β = 2.0 and β = 8.0' but does not list the intermediate values (presumably labelled only in Fig. 7). The text says the topologies remain almost identical, though Sec. 4.1.5 shows β can alter the layout.
Sec. 4.1 (Eq. 42 ff.) says the penalty r 'is increased in each iteration until it reaches a limit value r_max'. The initial multiplier λ, the initial r, the increase rule and r_max are never given.

Sec. 3 (Fig. 5 flowchart): the loop ends 'if convergence to a minimum is achieved, or a predefined number of iterations is reached'. Neither the tolerance nor the maximum number of iterations is stated; at most the iteration axis of Fig. 7 might show it.
readings: fixed 200 iterations
fixed 500 iterations
stop when the relative change of J < 1e-4 over 5 iterations and G ≤ 1e-3

items.entity: bounds on φ during the update
items.description: φ is defined to take values in [−1, 1] (Sec. 2.1), but the update (Eq. 32 / A.1) contains no truncation. The text never says whether φ is clipped after each step, as is done in reaction–diffusion level-set codes.
readings: clip φ to [−1, 1] after every update
no clipping (φ evolves freely)

items.description: Eq. 44 writes C_v = (1/(c_f V0)) ∫_D |∂R/∂Θ|_{L²(D)} dΩ, i.e. it integrates an L² norm over D. It is unclear whether C_v is the L² norm or the mean absolute value of the strain-energy sensitivity, and whether it is recomputed each iteration. With c_f = 1, C_v sets the step size of S_v = f_v β / C_v.
readings: C_v = ‖ε(u):∂τ/∂Θ C:ε(u)‖_{L²(D)} / c_f, recomputed every iteration
C_v = (1/(c_f V0)) ∫_D |ε(u):∂τ/∂Θ C:ε(u)| dΩ (mean absolute value), recomputed every iteration
either of the above, computed once at the first iteration and then kept fixed

items.entity: ersatz stiffness interpolation τ(Θ) and its derivative
items.description: Eq. 40 uses τ = (1−e)Θ^q + e (q = 3, e = 10^-3) with the smooth tanh Heaviside of Eq. 23. Eq. 41 then uses Θ^q ≡ Θ, which holds only for binary Θ, to get ∂τ/∂Θ = q(1−e)Θ. With a smooth Θ, the stiffness law and its sensitivity are inconsistent.
readings: τ = (1−e)Θ³ + e with the exact derivative 3(1−e)Θ²
τ = (1−e)Θ³ + e with the paper's derivative 3(1−e)Θ (Eq. 41)
τ = (1−e)Θ + e (identity also applied to the stiffness) with derivative 3(1−e)Θ

items.entity: initial level-set values φ0 and φ−1
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'a completely filled design domain serves as the initial configuration for both φ0 and φ−1'. It does not give the actual value of φ, and any positive constant counts as 'filled'. The value affects how quickly the undamped wave update reaches the zero level.
readings: φ0 = φ−1 = 1 everywhere
φ0 = φ−1 = 0.5 everywhere
φ0 = φ−1 = 0.1 everywhere
